scores.evidence: Phase 5 "Depends on: Phase 3 (retrieval, model access), Phase 4 (sandbox), Phase 2 (HITL gate on PR creation)."
scores.rationale: Each phase states explicit dependencies and the order runs from substrate (contracts, guardrails) to capabilities, with nothing specified before its prerequisite is proven.

scores.evidence: a person opens an issue in a dedicated sandbox repo... agent applies exactly one label from an allow-list and posts one comment
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real deployed end-to-end path from webhook to GitHub write, with tracing, a dashboard, an alert and a kill switch, and it has an exit check.

scores.evidence: Duplicate-action rate > 0.1%, or intake drops events during outages → add a durable intake buffer (SQS/PubSub)
scores.rationale: Nine irreversible decisions each carry a default and a concrete flip condition, up front.

scores.evidence: Tasks (widest → narrowest): 1. Permission model... 5. Action executor
scores.rationale: Every phase orders its tasks widest to narrowest, and the ordering is sensible, for example permissions and state before leaf work.

scores.evidence: 0 Skeleton | HMAC webhook verification; App key in KMS; enum-only LLM output; kill switch
scores.rationale: The cross-cutting table gives concrete security controls for every phase starting at Phase 0.

scores.evidence: An OpenTelemetry trace per delivery... Metrics: webhook_to_action_seconds, llm_tokens_total, llm_cost_usd... One dashboard and one alert
scores.rationale: Observability is concrete in Phase 0 and in every phase after.

scores.evidence: Terraform for all infra. The container image is built in CI and pinned by digest... prompt in git; model ID pinned
scores.rationale: Reproducibility is addressed concretely in every phase, from Terraform and pinned images to frozen eval sets and replayable attempts.

scores.evidence: Dedupe on delivery_id; 30s LLM timeout; failed jobs retried 3× with backoff, then marked failed (not lost)
scores.rationale: Each phase has specific failure handling, including idempotency, fallbacks, reapers, checkpoints and safe defaults.

scores.evidence: Phase 2 — Guardrails, budgets, human-in-the-loop (AI layer 1–3)... Phase 3 retrieval, model access; Phase 5 memory, orchestration; Phase 6 routing, feedback
scores.rationale: Defenses, budgets and HITL come first, then retrieval, model access, memory, orchestration, routing and feedback, matching the required order.

scores.evidence: Auto-merge | One fix class reaches ≥ 95% merge-without-edit over ≥ 200 PRs (autonomy gate).
scores.rationale: The deferred table lists items that are not being built, and each has a concrete pull-forward condition.

note: An exceptionally thorough plan that meets every rubric dimension with concrete content. One small nit is that Phase 0 uses an LLM call before the Phase 2 guardrails, but the Phase 0 controls (enum output, allow-list, caps, kill switch) cover that.
